sections.h2: What is Peach County, Georgia, like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Peach County is a small central Georgia county with Fort Valley as its seat and Byron as the second city. Its own website describes a place about 90 minutes south of Atlanta where big industry, small business and agriculture meet. Peach counted 29,877 people in the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, 6.7 percent more than its 2020 base. The land area is 150.28 square miles, which gave 186.2 people per square mile in 2020.

Homes here cost far less than in the Atlanta suburbs. Peach's median owner-occupied value is $207,800 (2020 to 2024), well under the Paulding and Pickens figures. Owner-occupancy of 69.6 percent is the lowest among the four counties compared, which makes rental houses a real part of the local market. Median gross rent was $940 and the median household income was $71,293. Builders pulled just 139 permits in 2025. Seniors make up 18.8 percent of the population, and workers spend a mean of 24.5 minutes getting to work, against 39.6 in Paulding County.

That mix of renters, older owners and modest values shapes the tax questions sellers ask. Many Peach County sellers have inherited a house, rented one out, or fallen behind on a bill. Poverty runs at 17.7 percent, and total employment was 7,571 in 2023, up 3.0 percent from the year before, so household budgets here can be tight. The tax offices described below can give a payoff figure in any of those situations.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Peach County property tax questions?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner bills and collects. The Board of Tax Assessors values property, takes exemption applications and handles appeals. Peach County's own assessor pages say the commissioner has no role in appraisal or in setting the millage rate, and that the county commissioners only appoint and fund the assessors.

The commissioner's office keeps Monday to Friday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Its site covers county tax only. The city tax page lists separate district codes for Byron, Fort Valley, Perry and Warner Robins, a reminder that parts of this county's tax base fall inside several city limits. If your house is inside one of those cities, ask that city's finance office about its separate bill.

sections.h2: When is Peach County property tax due?
sections.html:
December 20 is the customary deadline for real estate and business personal property, says the commissioner's FAQ. Mobile homes run on an April 1 schedule, and vehicle tax follows the primary owner's birthday. Dates can shift, so go by the one on your bill.

Late charges on real estate follow a simple schedule:

  • One percent interest accrues for each month the bill stays open.
  • Taxes still open 90 days after the deadline carry a one-time 10 percent penalty.
  • Owners with a homestead and a bill under $500 are exempt from that penalty.
  • An unpaid bill gives the commissioner both the authority and the responsibility to levy on the property.

The commissioner's home page has announced delinquent tax sales at the Peach County Courthouse at 205 W Church Street in Fort Valley, including one scheduled for March 3, 2026 at 10 a.m. The office posts a tax sale list for download. A seller who is behind should phone the Fort Valley office for a written balance before choosing a listing date.

sections.h2: How does a Peach County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
A new value you dispute can be challenged for 45 days after the notice date. Either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator takes the case. An owner who loses can go on to Superior Court by giving the assessors a written notice. The assessors' page cites O.C.G.A. 48-5-311 as the authority for the appeal.

Some facts about how Peach County measures value:

  • Assessed value runs at 40 percent of market value unless a statute sets another ratio (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Both the notice and the bill print the market value next to the assessed value.
  • The county's definition of market value is a price between an informed buyer and a willing seller who deal at arm's length.
  • Peach County says its assessors review property annually and may enter a parcel during business hours, with identification, to check data after a permit, a sale or an appeal.

Think about how a recent contract price compares with the notice before you contest a value on a house you plan to sell.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions apply in Peach County?
sections.html:
For the standard exemption, you must be living in the house as owner on January 1. Peach lists it as $2,000 subtracted from assessed value for state, county and school levies. Applications go to the Tax Assessor's Office. The county describes a filing period running from April 2 of the prior year to April 1 of the year the benefit is wanted.

The county's exemption page lists these programs:

  • A $4,000 reduction at age 65, for a household whose income the year before was $10,000 or less. Retirement, pension and disability payments are left out of that figure up to the Social Security cap.
  • Owners at 62 can add a school-tax reduction capped at $10,000 of assessed value, using the same $10,000 income ceiling.
  • A floating, inflation-proof option for households with income up to $30,000 and an owner of 62 or more. The county itself cautions that it may increase what you pay.
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, which the page lists at $109,986 for the 2023 tax year.

Bring proof of age, a warranty deed and income statements as the facts require. Refinancing, or any other deed change, requires a new application. A buyer files separately for the new home. Freeport exemptions for manufacturing and warehouse inventory are filed with the assessors by April 1.

sections.h2: How should a seller handle Peach County property tax at closing?
sections.html:
Call 478-825-3161 and ask what the parcel owes, including this year's tax, interest and anything left from earlier years. How the year's tax is split comes from your sale contract, and the settlement statement shows it.

If the buyer pays off a bill that includes city tax, remember that Fort Valley and Byron levy their own. Ask the commissioner whether the parcel is billed through the county alone or has a city component. Mobile homes are billed separately and are due April 1, so a manufactured home on the lot may carry its own balance.

The buyer needs to file a new homestead application after closing. After the sale, tell the assessors your exemption has ended. Peach asks owners to report any loss of eligibility.

faqs.q: When are Peach County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: According to the FAQ, December 20 is the standard due date for real estate. Mobile homes are due April 1, so confirm the exact date on your bill.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Peach County?
faqs.a: Interest of 1 percent monthly begins once the date passes, with a single 10 percent penalty at the 90-day point. A homesteaded home owing less than $500 escapes that penalty.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Peach County property value?
faqs.a: Counting starts on the notice date and stops at day 45. The hearing body is the Board of Equalization, or an arbitrator if chosen, with Superior Court above.

faqs.q: Who takes homestead applications in Peach County?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office in Fort Valley, with a warranty deed and any proof the exemption requires. The deadline to receive the benefit for the same year is April 1.

faqs.q: Does Peach County tax mobile homes?
faqs.a: Yes. Peach classes a mobile home as personal property, and the permit for its location waits on full payment of the April 1 bill.
